dedupe_keys.name: global maps of travel time to healthcare facilities malaria atlas project 2019

description: These global maps give the land-based travel time in minutes from every place to the nearest hospital or clinic, once assuming motorised transport and once walking only, together with the friction surfaces used to compute them. The facility layer merged OpenStreetMap, Google Maps and published academic facility lists, and the study found that 8.9% of the world's population cannot reach care within an hour with motorised transport and 43.3% cannot on foot. The producer is the Malaria Atlas Project, led by Daniel Weiss, with the Institute for Disease Modelling, Google, the European Commission Joint Research Centre and others (Nature Medicine, 2020). Coverage is global between 85 degrees north and 60 degrees south at about 1 km resolution for a nominal year 2019. GeoTIFF files download freely from the project page and the layers are in the Google Earth Engine catalogue, under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: facilities are not distinguished by capability, travel speeds are generalised by land cover and road class, ferries and border delays are simplified, and the maps are a static snapshot. Simulation uses: baseline accessibility for hazard scenarios in which roads or facilities fail, equity weighting of health service disruption, and siting of new facilities. Related records: AccessMod (model-accessmod) computes the same kind of surface for national studies, and Healthsites.io (data-healthsites-io) supplies facility points.
